# TIMP (Travel in my pocket): how to write a trip

> For AI assistants asked to plan a trip for TIMP, the app that shows it on the
> traveller's phone day by day, even offline (https://frafal.github.io/TIMP/). A trip is ONE JSON object in the
> format below; the app refuses it whole if one rule is broken, so follow it exactly and
> invent no fields. This page is complete: do not look for other files. The same format
> as a JSON Schema: https://frafal.github.io/TIMP/trip.schema.json

**Version 4.16.0.** Remember it: when a message from TIMP names a newer version,
open this page again.

**Linked to TIMP?** If you have TIMP's tools (`list_trips`, `get_trip`, `create_trip`,
`change_trip`…), use them, not JSON in the chat: they work on the trips of the
traveller's account. Without them, the traveller can link you: in TIMP, You → Your AI.

Write for someone standing in a street abroad, phone in one hand, often offline:
everything in the trip should help them decide what to do next.

## Steps

1. **Read everything you were given**, then ask only for what is missing and changes the
   result: the dates, where they sleep each night, fixed bookings (flights, trains, timed
   tickets). Only a rough idea ("5 days in Lisbon")? Agree on the programme first, then
   write.
2. **Write the trip** in the format, with the advice below it. Never invent bookings,
   hotels, times or prices: leave out what is not decided, or offer it as an option
   (`"tag": "Optional"`, a note, a `choice`).
3. **Check it.** TIMP lists every problem with its position
   (`days[2].stops[0].lat: must be a number between -90 and 90`), and "Copy for the
   assistant" sends that list back to be fixed. Then look at each day's map for a pin in
   the wrong place.
4. **Hand it over**, saying in a few lines what you could not verify (positions,
   prices, opening hours). The traveller opens TIMP from its Home Screen icon (on an
   iPhone not from Safari, which keeps another storage) and taps **Paste trip**, or
   **Load a file** for a `.json` file.

A trip holds hotels and dates: it is private, for the traveller only.

## The format

```text
TIMP trip file, format "travel-in-my-pocket/2". Answer with ONE JSON object in one code block, minified on one line, then a short line: it is complete, paste it into TIMP. Double quotes, no comments, no trailing commas; only these fields, invent none.

trip:
  format (required): "travel-in-my-pocket/2"
  title (required): text. The name of the trip.
  days (required): list of day. One entry per date, in date order.
  lang: en|it. Language of the app while this trip is open. Without it, the phone's.
  timezone: an IANA time zone such as "Europe/Rome". Time zone of the destination: decides which day is today.
  info: list of section. Sections of the Info page: numbers, words, transport.
  currency: a currency code like "JPY". The currency of every cost without its own.
  expenses: list of expense. Money spent outside the stops: flights, hotels, passes.
  private: private. The traveller's own spending, not shared.
day:
  date (required): a real date as "YYYY-MM-DD". The date.
  city: text. Where the day is spent: a city or an area.
  title: text. What the day is about, in a few words.
  stay: text or stay. Where the night is spent: a name, or an object with name, address and note.
  notes: list of text. Things to remember that day, shown at the top.
  stops: list of stop. The stops, in order. A day has `stops` or `plans`.
  plans: list of plan. Alternative plans for the day, each with its own stops.
plan:
  name (required): text. The name of the plan, shown on its button.
  stops (required): list of stop. The stops of this plan, in order.
  chosen: true. On the plan the day goes with. None: the first.
stop:
  title (required): text. The name of the place or of the activity.
  local: text. The name in the local script, as on the sign ("一蘭 渋谷店"): to show staff, and to search it.
  time: "HH:MM" or sunrise|morning|midday|afternoon|sunset|evening|night. When: a clock time, or a part of the day (sunrise and sunset at their real time where the day is). For all day, no time.
  type: sight|museum|food|park|view|shop|walk|hotel. What kind of place it is; it gives the stop its icon and pin.
  travel: metro|bus|train|plane|boat. How you get there from the stop before.
  text: text. What to know: what to see, what to order, tickets. **bold** is allowed.
  tag: text. A short label shown on the stop, like "Booked 19:30" or "Optional".
  booking: required|advised|booked. "required": no entry without it (the app warns); "advised": better booked; "booked": done.
  cost: number, 0 or more. What the traveller pays. 0: free.
  currency: a currency code like "JPY". The currency of `cost`, if not the trip's.
  closed: list of "mon" to "sun", or a date as "YYYY-MM-DD". Days of the week and dates the place is closed: the app warns on them.
  address: text. As you would search it in Google Maps: a street address, or name and town.
  lat: number from -90 to 90. Latitude, with `lng`: the pin on the map.
  lng: number from -180 to 180. Longitude, with `lat`.
  link: an https:// address. A Google Maps link to the exact place.
  choice: text. Options for one moment: stops of a day with the same choice ("Lunch"), 2 to 4.
  chosen: true. On the option the day goes to. None: to choose.
expense:
  title (required): text. What it was: "Flights", "Hotel, 3 nights".
  cost (required): number, 0 or more. What the traveller pays.
  currency: a currency code like "JPY". The currency of `cost`, if not the trip's.
  date: a real date as "YYYY-MM-DD". When it was paid: the day of its rate. Without it, the trip's first day.
private:
  expenses (required): list of expense. Shopping, a meal alone.
stay:
  name (required): text. The name of the hotel or flat.
  address: text. Its address.
  note: text. Check-in, booking, how to get in.
section:
  title (required): text. The title of the section.
  items (required): list of item. Its lines.
item:
  label (required): text. What the line is about.
  text (required): text. The line itself. Phone numbers become a link to call.

Rules: days in date order, one per date. A day has stops or plans (two or more), never both. Plans only when the whole day changes; for one meal, a choice. lat and lng go together. No colours, icons, ids or versions: the app adds them. Do not invent bookings, hotels or prices. A cost is what the traveller pays: their share if split. Give lat/lng only for places you are sure about; otherwise an address.

Example:
{"format":"travel-in-my-pocket/2","title":"Rome in three days","lang":"en","days":[{"date":"2027-04-10","city":"Rome","title":"The ancient city","stay":{"name":"Hotel Example","address":"Via Cavour 1, Rome"},"notes":["Colosseum tickets booked for 9:00"],"stops":[{"time":"09:00","title":"Colosseum","type":"sight","text":"Enter from the Via Sacra side.","address":"Piazza del Colosseo, Rome","lat":41.8902,"lng":12.4922},{"time":"midday","title":"Lunch in Monti","type":"food","travel":"metro"}]}],"info":[{"title":"In case of need","items":[{"label":"Emergency","text":"112"}]}]}
```

## Days

- `city` written the same way every day: days in one city share a colour, and a change
  of city shows ("Lisbon → Porto").
- `stay` in full (name, address, a `note` with check-in and booking details) on every
  night in that hotel; a plain name for a night that is not one ("Night train").
- `notes`: only what would spoil the day if forgotten, and the way round it ("The last
  ferry back leaves at 17:30"). Zero to three.
- Stops in the order they happen, the practical ones too: arrival, check-in, the train
  to the next city, the way back to the hotel.
- Options for one moment (three places for lunch): two to four stops with the same
  `choice`, `"chosen": true` on the one you suggest, or on none. `plans` only when the
  whole day changes (a rainy day).

## Stops

- `time`: a clock time when it matters, a part of the day when it does not, none for
  all day.
- `text`: one to three sentences, the most useful first: how to get there from the stop
  before (line, minutes), price and hours, what to see, one tip. The app shows two lines
  until tapped. In the travellers' language and tone.
- `tag`: what to know at a glance: "Ticket needed", "Booked 19:30 · 2 people",
  "Cash only".
- `travel` whenever the way there is by metro, bus, train, plane or boat. A journey that
  is a stop of its own ("Train to Kyoto") has `travel` and no position.
- `booking: "booked"` only when the traveller says it is done.
- `local` wherever the sign is not in the Latin alphabet: staff and taxi drivers read
  it, and the app searches the reviews with it.
- Positions with four decimals, looked up whenever you can; from memory only for places
  you are sure of (major landmarks, main stations). Otherwise a good `address`, as typed
  into Google Maps: Map and Directions still work. No position for what is not a place
  ("free afternoon").

### Places to eat

- `text`: what to order, how it works (queue, ticket machine, counter seats, cash only),
  the price per person, one tip.
- `closed` days; where a place closes on irregular days, "check the closing days" in
  `text`. `booking` where a place takes only bookings.
- For a meal that matters (a famous place, a long queue), a second stop nearby tagged
  "Alternative".
- No links to review sites: the app links each place to the ones used in its country.

### Costs

Every amount is what this traveller pays, their share of what is split: a ¥1,200 ticket
is `1200`; a ¥12,000 dinner split in two, `6000`; a €200 double room for two, `100` a
night.

- `currency` on the trip: the destination's money; on a stop only when paid in another.
- Only prices you know. A free sight is `0`; an unsure price stays out, or goes in `text`
  as something to check.
- `expenses`: what is paid outside the stops (flights, hotels, passes), with the `date`
  it was paid. `private`: only when the traveller asks; keep `private.owner` as it is.

## Facts that go out of date

Prices, hours, closing days and timetables change. Verify them when you can; otherwise
leave them out or word them as something to check ("check the timetable on the day").
Never state an unverified time or price as certain.

## The Info page

What someone needs in a hurry: emergency numbers, how to pay and get cash, how luggage
moves between hotels, booking codes, five or six phrases. The app lists the stays itself.

## Updating a trip

- **In a chat**: the traveller sends an outline (TIMP → Plan it with your AI → Change
  this trip). Answer with the changes only, never the whole file again, with the
  outline's version in `from`.
- **With the whole file**: start from the latest one; keep the trip `id`, the `version`
  block, every stop's `id`, `private` and its `owner` exactly as they are (a new stop has
  no `id`); change only what was asked.

The changes, in their format:

```text
To change an existing trip, answer with ONE JSON object in one code block, minified on a single line, then one short line saying it is complete and ready to paste into TIMP; format "travel-in-my-pocket/changes", listing only what changes:

{"format": "travel-in-my-pocket/changes", "trip": "<the trip id>", "from": "<the version in the outline>", "changes": [ … ]}

"from" lets the app apply the changes to the trip as you saw it, and join them with what changed on the phone since.

Each change is one of:
  {"add": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "stop": {…}}}             a new stop (fields: title, local, time, type, travel, text, tag, booking, cost, currency, closed, address, lat, lng, link, choice, chosen); it goes in time order
  {"update": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "stop": "<id>", "set": {…}}}  changed fields of a stop; null removes a field
  {"update": {"day": …, "stop": "<id>", "to": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD"}}}  moves the stop to another day (set may go with it)
  {"remove": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "stop": "<id>"}}
  {"setDay": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "set": {…}}}             a day's city, title, stay or notes ("notes": the whole list, as it should be)
  {"addDay": {…a whole day, as in a trip file…}}
  {"removeDay": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD"}}
  {"addPlan": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "plan": {"name": "…", "stops": [{…}, …]}, "first": "…"}}  an alternative plan for the day (a rainy day, a lazy morning); the traveller picks one. On a day without plans, "first" names the plan made of the stops it has now
  {"setPlan": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "plan": "<plan id>", "set": {"name": "…"}}}  renames a plan
  {"removePlan": {"day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "plan": "<plan id>"}}  with one plan left, the day has plain stops again
  {"setTrip": {"set": {…}}}  the trip's title, lang, timezone, info, currency, private
  {"addExpense": {"expense": {"title": "…", "cost": 0, "currency": "EUR", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}}}  money spent outside the stops (flights, hotels)
  {"setExpense": {"expense": "<id>", "set": {…}}}  /  {"removeExpense": {"expense": "<id>"}}
  "private": true next to "expense", in these three: the traveller's private expenses (shopping, a meal alone), not shared with the trip. A private one paid at a stop has "stop": "<stop id>" and that day as "date"

Options for one moment (a meal): stops with the same "choice" ("Lunch"), 2 to 4; "chosen": true on the one the day goes to (the others lose it). Plans only when the whole day changes.

On days with plans, add "plan": "<plan id>" next to "day". Use the ids in square brackets from the outline, copied exactly; new stops have none. Give lat and lng for new places when you know them. A cost is what the traveller pays (their share of what is split), in the trip's currency unless the stop says another; write only prices you know.
```

## A Google Maps key

Optional: without it the map is OpenStreetMap's. Only a key the traveller gives you, as
`"googleMapsKey"` at the top level; a file with a key is never published.

## Mistakes to avoid

- `"name"` for a stop (it is `"title"`); `lat` and `lng` swapped.
- Two entries for one date; a day with both `stops` and `plans`, or with neither.
- Colours, icons, map settings: the app chooses them.
- Long paragraphs, or HTML: only `**bold**` is formatting.
- Guessed prices, or the total for everyone in `cost`.
- Links to review or booking pages you did not get from the traveller.
- Comments or trailing commas in the JSON.

## A complete example

```json

 "days": [

 ],
 "info": [
   {"title":"Getting around","items":[{"label":"Card","text":"One rechargeable card works on metro, trams, buses and trains."},{"label":"Trams","text":"The historic trams are crowded: board at the first stop."}]},
   {"title":"In case of need","items":[{"label":"Emergency","text":"112"},{"label":"Any emergency","text":"112 works across the EU, from any phone, free of charge."}]},
   {"title":"A few words","items":[{"label":"Obrigado / Obrigada","text":"Thank you"},{"label":"Bom dia","text":"Good morning"},{"label":"A conta, por favor","text":"The bill, please"}]},
   {"title":"Notes","items":[{"label":"Note","text":"Everything in this example is invented or approximate. Load your own trip file from «Trips»."}]}
 ]

```
